comments.text:
I am a food runner at a resturant at a hotel in the midwest.  I am like the last lady.  I start my shift I prepare a hot sani bucket with soap as well.  I get clean microfibers from housekeeping that have been washed in bleach.  I replace all dirty microfibers at the bar used to polish with clean ones.  I wipe down every table to my standard of cleanliness, which is impeccable.  I throw away anything that has been sitting out, I "burn" the ice bins and clean them with hot water and soap.  Today when I go in I will wash the ice buckets.  I polish the silverware in hot water.  I also wash my hands everytime I go back in the kitchen after I run food or clear a table.  It's for my protection and yours.  I wear gloves when bussing and throw them away after I drop off the dirty plates and then still wash my hands.  

I have seen my co workers use the bathroom and not wash their hands which is gross.  I have seen them walk over spills, I have seen them put dirty glasses and move them over the clean ice bins.  My hotel is pretty good but I still try to go the extra mile.  I was saying to someone that they dont realize how dirty resturants really are, and how many people truly dont care about food safety.  Good thing for me, I don't have a social life and I have food allergies, so I cook everything at home from scratch and I pour my own drinks from the comfort of my clean kitchen.
